messages:
anya: quick heads-up about a new autoscale idea: switch from qps-led to a headroom-token model driven by runtime p95. sketch below, want quick sanity check.

leo: curious. how are tokens issued and consumed?

anya: control-plane computes soft_headroom per-tenant and calls operator SetHeadroom(tenant, n, ttl). operator returns tokens. requests tagged with a token get routed to prewarmed slots. if token use rate is high we convert -> strong reserve.

pranav: sounds reasonable. concerns: p95 noise -> oscillation, and simultaneous stampede across tenants.

maria: telemetry: agree we must use runtime p95 measured after the KV/cache layer. proxies add network noise. i'll write the spec for the metric and the tags.

leo: mitigation ideas: require 2 consecutive breach windows to scale up, 3 cooldowns to scale down. cap growth rate (e.g. +20% nodes/min). randomize TTL jitter to avoid coordinated retries.

anya: also propose cache_miss_multiplier: if miss_rate > 0.1, multiply soft_headroom by 2. simple heuristic but helps bursty cache-miss traffic.

pranav: fairness: enforce per-tenant soft fraction cap (e.g. 15% of pool) and global soft cap. prioritization: SLA tier -> recent usage -> rand.

infra-bot: rollout plan: canary in us-west-2 dedicated pools, feature-flag: headroom_tokens_v1. alert: runtime_p95 > target+30ms for 2m => rollback.

maria: billing note: prewarm tokens must be metered/tagged. either bill discounted prewarm minutes or tag for internal chargeback.

anya: next actions: i'll draft RFC for API + DSL + rollout. leo/pranav/maria volunteer to co-author. i'll link PR here when ready. :thumbsup:
